messages:
Maya (Support): Customer AcmeAI reports intermittent 502/504s for hosted generation streams. Failures consistently happen ~30-90s into the stream. Request-ID: req-95a1c4f2. Customer is blocked — they can reproduce with curl. Can someone triage?

Ben (Eng-SRE): Can you paste the curl repro + full response headers and any trace ids? Also: did anything change on the auth side for that tenant? Is non-streaming generation affected?

Maya (Support): Repro curl below (sanitized keys):
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_xxx" -H "Content-Type: application/json" https://api.redwood.inference/v1/generate -d '{
  "model":"rw-text-2-large",
  "stream":true,
  "prompt":"<very long prompt causing 6-7k tokens>"
}'
```
Response snippet from customer: 
```
< HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
< content-type: application/json
< x-request-id: req-95a1c4f2
{"error":{"message":"upstream reset"}}
```
Customer said retrying with stream=false succeeds. Observed at 2026-02-15T17:34:23Z on their side.

Carol (Edge): I pulled the traces for req-95a1c4f2 — pattern: client opens stream, large response tokens emitted, then midproxy resets connection to upstream around ~30s later. Envoy logs show: `upstream reset: stream error: reason: FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR` for the upstream connection. Also I see an auth token rotation event for tenant acmeai at ~17:34:30Z.

Ben (Eng-SRE): Interesting. Need metrics: p99 connection durations, active h2 streams, and any pod restarts / autoscale events for the midproxy group around 17:30-17:40. Can someone attach kube events and envoy stats for that window? Also request a tcpdump for the exact ReqID for 5s around the reset.

Dave (Infra): No global network flaps. We did autoscale the midproxy ASG at 17:29–17:31 and a couple of pods cycled. That could cause connection churn. I'll pull kube events and correlate restarts to the request timeline.

Maya (Support): Pasting minimal customer log snippet and our edge log entries for the req: 
```
[17:34:23] edge/nginx[pid]: stream opened req=req-95a1c4f2 tenant=acmeai
[17:34:55] edge/nginx[pid]: upstream reset id=req-95a1c4f2 err=RST_STREAM code=2
[17:34:56] auth/cache: tenant token rotated tenant=acmeai new=tok-rot-17:34
```
Customer notes it only happens with very long prompts / high token output. Short requests are fine.

Carol (Edge): Correlating logs: token rotation + pod churn + long-lived streaming connections = bad combo. Hypothesis: midproxy reused a pooled connection where the server-side had rotated auth state and closed the stream; because the stream was long and flow-controlled it produced a FLOW_CONTROL/RESET instead of a clean close, surfacing as 502 to client. Also large payloads expose h2 window behavior and buffer exhaustion in this codepath.

Ben (Eng-SRE): Mitigations:
1) Short-term: ask customer to retry non-streaming or reconnect on reset (we already recommend backoff).
2) Short-term infra change: disable connection reuse for tenant acmeai (force a fresh handshake on each new stream) so token rotation won't affect in-flight streams.
3) Mid-term: add a guard in midproxy to detect token rotations and gracefully drain long streams or proactively reject with 429 so callers can reconnect.

Carol (Edge): I can flip an ingress flag: `ingress.disable_conn_reuse: acmeai=true` and bump midproxy replicas to 4 to reduce load. Will roll the config to two pods first, monitor.

Dave (Infra): I'll add an autoscale safety rule so when midproxy is scaling, we temporarily reduce concurrent long stream acceptance or mark pods as draining before termination. Also will collect the requested pcap.

Maya (Support): Notified customer of the plan and asked them to retry. They attempted a non-streaming request and it succeeded. They agreed to a short window of testing while we roll the change.

Ben (Eng-SRE): Action items: collect pcap for req-95a1c4f2, pod logs (+ envoy stats) for midproxy group, and kube events for autoscale. Also add a test that simulates token rotation while streaming high-length outputs.

Carol (Edge): Flag flipped at 17:45:10Z. After the change 502/504 rate for long-stream requests from acmeai dropped to near zero in the following 10m window. Will keep monitoring and follow up with a proper code fix.

Maya (Support): Customer reports immediate improvement. Setting status to "monitoring" and will keep the case open for 24h. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: config/ingress updated for tenant=acmeai by carol at 2026-02-15T17:45:10Z

Ben (Eng-SRE): Follow-ups (owner assignments):
- Carol: implement a graceful-drain on token rotation for long streams (P0), add feature flag tests.
- Dave: add autoscale drain rule + collect PCAPs.
- Maya: keep customer updated and confirm 24h clean window before close.

Maya (Support): Closing note — verified improvements, customer will do broader load test tomorrow. Keeping thread open until no recurrence for 24h.
